subject: Clarify: default log treatment for requests vs generated outputs
messages:
From: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Default log retention — quick clarifications for procurement

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our procurement/security team has a few quick clarifications on Redwood's default capture policy before we proceed with the security questionnaire. Specifically: 1) Are raw requests (customer-supplied prompts) retained by default in hosted deployments, or treated as ephemeral? 2) Are generated model outputs (responses/completions) kept by default? 3) Do streaming chunks get persisted as full responses, or only reconstructed after completion?

We appreciate short, actionable answers — we will follow up with the formal SOC2 evidence request if everything looks good.

Regards,
Ethan Li
Security Engineer, BrightBank
E: ethan.li@brightbank.com
T: +44 20 5555 1234

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Li <ethan.li@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Default log retention — quick clarifications for procurement

Ethan —

Short answers up front, followed by a slightly expanded explanation for each point:

1) Raw requests (prompts/input): By default in our hosted API, customer-submitted prompt text is captured for 45 days for debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.

2) Generated outputs (responses/completions): Outputs are kept by default for the same 45-day baseline. We treat prompts and completions as part of the session artifacts.

3) Streaming behavior: Streaming tokens are reconstructed into the final response and stored as a single output artifact; partial streaming fragments are not individually persisted.

Notes: These are the default hosted API settings — customers can opt into shorter retention, enable automatic purge, or choose Dedicated/Private modes (where retention defaults can be configured by the customer).

I'll attach the retention matrix that maps our default capture windows and available overrides. Kim and Marissa are looped in for procurement/security follow-ups.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachment: retention-matrix.xlsx (internal matrix mapping capture windows)
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Default log retention — quick clarifications for procurement

Ethan —

A couple of procurement-focused clarifications to add:

• Defaults are 45 days for hosted. For Dedicated we provide a customer-configurable retention window as part of the contract. For Private (VPC/on-prem) the customer fully controls storage and purge policies.

• Export & deletion: We support on-demand export of artifacts (CSV/JSON) and a documented erase flow — customers can request immediate purge for specific tokens/artifacts and we provide an audit entry once purge completes.

• Encryption and residency: Data at rest is encrypted by default and stored in the region of the tenancy. For BrightBank (EU region) artifacts are kept in eu-west-1. KMS-backed keys are available for Dedicated/Private.

Let us know if you need SOC2 evidence; I can coordinate delivery of relevant control artifacts and an export of the retention configuration that would apply to your account (BD-3421).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups before we close the loop:

1) Can you confirm whether prompt text ever goes into long-term analytics stores (beyond the 45-day window) for aggregated telemetry or model improvement unless the customer opts in? We need an explicit no to satisfy our policy.

2) For streaming, if a session fails mid-stream and the customer retries, is the partial attempt retained anywhere (for debugging) or automatically purged as incomplete?

If you can confirm in writing we will mark this item resolved and proceed with the procurement checklist. Also, Marissa — if there are any standard commercial concessions (e.g., data-retention SLAs or shorter default windows) that BrightBank should be aware of, flag them and we can evaluate during contract redline.
